name: Canvas 2D
role: Immediate-mode 2D raster drawing; redraw each frame as a pure function of t
summary: The browser's 2D drawing context: paths, text, gradients, images, compositing and pixel access, supported in every Chromium. VCR draws a frame by clearing and redrawing from t, then screenshots or reads pixels, so output is deterministic given fixed fonts and assets. Nothing is retained between frames, which suits generative work and rules out a scene graph.
use_when: Generative or data-driven 2D redrawn each frame from t, no scene graph needed
Over SVG when hundreds of shapes move or pixel manipulation is needed
Over PixiJS when the scene is small and you want zero dependencies
avoid_when: Thousands of sprites or filters: PixiJS on WebGL
Editable vector text and logos: SVG
Interactive scenes with hit testing: Konva or Fabric.js
notes: 2026-10-26: Font-load timing before the first frame affects canvas text; not tested here.

assessment.rationale: Standard-track, not experimental, supported since Chrome 1 per MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.7; no VCR-specific gaps known. Canvas text depends on fonts being loaded.
